chapter: Topic-based: use with whichever Class 9 book your students follow
title: Quick Revision: Force and Laws of Motion

table: Equal and opposite forces; no change in the state of motion
A net force; it changes speed or direction (causes acceleration)
The tendency of a body to resist a change in its state of rest or motion. Mass is a measure of inertia.
p = mv. A vector, in kg m/s
The force that gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m/s^{2}

bullets: **First law:** a body stays at rest, or in uniform motion in a straight line, unless an unbalanced force acts on it (law of inertia).
**Second law:** the rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied force, in the direction of the force: **F = ma**.
**Third law:** to every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. **Action and reaction act on different bodies**, so they never cancel.

box: **Conservation of momentum:** m_{1}u_{1} + m_{2}u_{2} = m_{1}v_{1} + m_{2}v_{2} (total momentum before = after, if no external force)

bullets: Passengers lurch forward when a bus stops suddenly; beating a carpet removes dust: **inertia**.
A fielder pulls the hands back while catching: more time, so a smaller force (second law).
Gun recoil, rockets, swimming, walking: **third law**. Seat belts reduce injury by slowing us down over a longer time.
Using grams instead of kg, or km/h instead of m/s, in F = ma.
Saying action and reaction cancel. They act on different objects.
